policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the SBLGNT reading.

decisions.evidence: ASV 'Now even the first covenant had ordinances' renders an adverbial kai ('even') qualifying 'the first'; men oun alone accounts for 'Now' but leaves 'even' without a Greek word, so the reading with kai is the one rendered.
The readings differ only in the Greek articles; ASV 'the Holy of holies' is the same English either way, and no note is mapped here.
The variant is the gender of the relative pronoun (feminine agreeing with the parable, masculine with the time); ASV 'according to which' is ambiguous in English and picks out neither antecedent.

ASV parenthesizes '(with meats and drinks and divers washings)' and makes 'carnal ordinances' the predicate of 'being only', which requires the nominative dikaiomata; the dative dikaiomasin would join the parenthesized list, so r02 is excluded. The remaining readings differ only by kai, which the English does not settle.
ASV 'the good things to come' renders mellonton; the mapped textual_variant note 'Some ancient authorities read the good things that are come' relegates genomenon to the margin.
ASV 'the blood of goats and bulls' follows the order tragon kai tauron; the RP reading reverses the two nouns.
ASV 'cleanse your conscience' renders hymon, and the mapped textual_variant note 'Many ancient authorities read our' places hemon in the margin.

ASV 'it doth never avail' renders mepote ('never'); the marginal question 'Or, for doth it ever . . . liveth?' is the same word taken interrogatively. The split me tote would give 'not then', which the ASV does not render.
The variant is the presence of the Greek article with 'law'; ASV 'according to the law' reads the same whether or not the article stood, and no note is mapped here.

ASV 'the blood of the calves and the goats' names the goats, so the shorter reading without kai tragon is excluded; the two longer readings differ only in the article before 'goats', which the English does not distinguish.
The readings differ in Greek word order and in the article with Christ; ASV 'For Christ entered not into a holy place made with hands' carries neither distinction into English.
nyni and nyn are the same adverb with and without the emphatic iota; ASV 'but now' renders either, and the two mapped notes are alternative_rendering notes about other words.
The variant is the article with hamartias; ASV 'to put away sin' is the same English with or without it, and the mapped notes are alternative_rendering notes about other words.
